title: Detailed HTTP Request and Response Analysis knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which security principle best applies to “Detailed HTTP Request and Response Analysis”?
options: Rely on a hidden frontend control and skip backend verification because normal users cannot see the route.
Disable logs and tests so the security check cannot generate false positives.
Trust caller-controlled values and verify the control only on the successful happy path.
Inspect the relevant request, browser, transport, or architecture boundary; configure the narrow control required and verify the result in a controlled environment.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the relevant request, browser, transport, or architecture boundary; configure the narrow control required and verify the result in a controlled environment.
questions.explanation: Inspect the relevant request, browser, transport, or architecture boundary; configure the narrow control required and verify the result in a controlled environment. The other choices rely on obscurity, remove useful verification, or trust input that should be treated as untrusted.

questions.prompt: You are reviewing “Detailed HTTP Request and Response Analysis” in an application you own or an explicitly authorized local lab. Which approach gives the strongest evidence that the intended control works?
options: Run broad tests against unrelated public systems to find a comparison point.
Record real credentials and tokens in the report to make reproduction easier.
Write a focused test for the expected secure behavior and at least one relevant denied, malformed, expired, or failure case; record sanitized evidence.
Test only by looking at the page design and assume hidden controls are enforced.
questions.answer_key: Write a focused test for the expected secure behavior and at least one relevant denied, malformed, expired, or failure case; record sanitized evidence.
questions.explanation: A useful security check has a defined scope, expected behavior, negative/failure coverage, and sanitized evidence. Never expand testing beyond permission or store secrets in evidence.

questions.prompt: If a check related to “Detailed HTTP Request and Response Analysis” fails unexpectedly, what is the best next step?
options: Suppress the finding without documenting why it is a false positive.
Reproduce with synthetic test data, compare expected and actual behavior, identify the root cause, apply a targeted fix, and retest neighboring paths.
Declare the entire application secure after a single successful request.
Change several unrelated settings at once and do not save the test conditions.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce with synthetic test data, compare expected and actual behavior, identify the root cause, apply a targeted fix, and retest neighboring paths.
questions.explanation: Reducing the case and retaining reproducible sanitized evidence supports root-cause analysis. A targeted regression test helps prevent the issue from returning.
